name: FSRS Flashcards GPT Action
description: ChatGPT GPT Action integration for the FSRS spaced-repetition flashcard service (D:/fsrs). Lets ChatGPT create, bulk-create, list, get due, review, read, update, bulk-update, delete, and bulk-delete flashcards, manage decks (create/list/get/update/delete), attach images by URL or upload images to Firebase Storage, and list/remove card images, and run persistent review sessions (start/get/submit/end) via the Firebase backend.
statusNote: This GPT Action (Custom GPT + OpenAPI schema) is superseded by the MCP server in mcp-server/ (ChatGPT Apps SDK platform: Streamable HTTP at /mcp). This manifest is kept as a migration reference for the deployed backend contract. See mcp-server/README.md for the current integration and chatgpt/README.md for the migration note. Do not configure new Custom GPTs from this directory.
integrationSurfaceNote: Legacy ChatGPT Plugins (ai-plugin.json, OpenAPI 3.0 + x-openai-isConsequential era) were retired in April 2024. The GPT Action surface documented here is itself now superseded by the MCP server in mcp-server/. This manifest is repo metadata for maintainers only; OpenAI consumes the OpenAPI schema (openapi.yaml) plus the editor-configured auth.

server.note: The backend deploys each handler as a SEPARATE named Cloud Function (functions/src/index.ts): health, createFlashcardHandler, bulkCreateFlashcardsHandler, listFlashcardsHandler, dueFlashcardsHandler, reviewFlashcardHandler, getFlashcardHandler, updateFlashcardHandler, deleteFlashcardHandler, bulkUpdateFlashcardsHandler, bulkDeleteFlashcardsHandler, createDeckHandler, listDecksHandler, getDeckHandler, updateDeckHandler, deleteDeckHandler, migrateDecksHandler, attachImageHandler, uploadImageHandler, listImagesHandler, removeImageHandler, startReviewSessionHandler, getReviewSessionHandler, submitSessionReviewHandler, endReviewSessionHandler. There is no /api router prefix; card/deck/session ids are path suffixes on the function URLs. Replace <project-id> with the real Firebase project id before configuring the GPT Action.

auth.name: X-API-Key
auth.enforcement: Backend enforces the X-API-Key header only when NODE_ENV=production (see functions/src/index.ts authenticateRequest); local dev/emulator is unauthenticated. health is always public.
auth.configuredIn: GPT editor → Configure → Authentication → API Key
auth.note: Keys are validated against the Firestore apiKeys collection (key = document id, revoked flag honored). OpenAI stores keys encrypted. In the MCP server (mcp-server/) this same key is read from the environment (CUELINGUA_API_KEY) and forwarded server-side; it is never exposed to ChatGPT.

operations.summary: Check service reachability (public)
Create a flashcard
Atomically create up to 100 flashcards in one request (single Firestore batch; all-or-nothing)
List flashcards (filters: deck, tags ANY-of; pagination: pageSize, pageToken)
Get flashcards due for review now (new + scheduled, earliest first; optional deck filter + pagination)
Record an FSRS review rating (1=Again, 2=Hard, 3=Good, 4=Easy); returns updated card + review log entry
Get one flashcard
Update a flashcard (partial)
Atomically update up to 100 existing flashcards by id (single Firestore transaction; all-or-nothing; missing ids omitted)
Delete a flashcard
Atomically delete up to 100 flashcards by id (single Firestore transaction; all-or-nothing; missing ids omitted)
Create a deck (unique name); cards reference decks by stable deckId
List decks (pageSize/pageToken pagination)
Get one deck
Update a deck (name/description; rename rewrites the name on its cards)
Delete a deck — destructive to the deck but NOT its cards (cards reassigned to Uncategorized)
Maintenance: backfill deckId from legacy deck names
Attach an image to a flashcard by URL (validated http(s), allowed MIME/extension, <=5 per card; URL reference metadata only, never image bytes)
Upload an image (base64) to a flashcard; bytes go to Firebase Storage, card stores cloud metadata (id/storagePath/downloadUrl/contentType/sizeBytes/alt/addedAt); <=10 MiB, raster MIME only (no SVG)
List a flashcard's image attachments (URL refs + cloud metadata: id, storagePath, downloadUrl, sizeBytes)
Remove an image attachment by its exact URL (removes only the card's reference, not the external file)
Start a persistent review session: snapshot the currently due cards (optional deckId, limit 1-100 default 100, ordered earliest due first); returns session + first card
Get a review session (any status) plus its current card; only the starting API key can read it
Rate the session's expected current card (1-4, optional reviewAt); atomically applies FSRS and advances the session; returns session + next card
End an active review session without rating the rest (idempotent; status -> ended)

create.deck: string (optional legacy deck name, find-or-create; absent = Uncategorized deck)
create.deckId: string (optional, stable deck reference from decks collection; absent = Uncategorized deck)

bulkCreate.note: All items validated before any write; committed as one Firestore batch (no partial success).

bulkUpdate.body: { cards: [{ id, front?, back?, deck?, tags? }] } — at most 100 items
bulkUpdate.response: 200 { cards: Flashcard[] } (input order; missing ids omitted)
bulkUpdate.note: Scheduling fields (state/stability/difficulty/reps/lapses/due/reviewLog) are never accepted; reads+writes run in one Firestore transaction (no partial success).

bulkDelete.note: Existence checked in one Firestore transaction (no partial success).

read.deck: string (optional) — denormalized deck name, kept coherent on rename
read.reviewLog: array of ReviewLogEntry {rating, state, review, due, stability, difficulty, reps, lapses}
read.images: CardImage[] (optional) — { id, url, alt?, mimeType?, addedAt, storagePath?, downloadUrl?, sizeBytes? } (external: URL reference only; cloud uploads: full metadata incl. storagePath/downloadUrl/sizeBytes)

review.reviewAt: string ISO-8601 datetime, optional (defaults to server time)

sessions.model: ReviewSession { id, apiKeyName, status (active|completed|ended), mode (spaced_repetition), deckId?, limit (fixed 100), dueCount (exact due count at start), cardIds, currentIndex, reviewedCount, remainingCount, truncated, continuationAvailable (true when >100 due at start), ratingCounts {again,hard,good,easy,ratingCounts}, startedAt, lastReviewedAt?, endedAt? }
sessions.limits: max 100 cards per session (MAX_SESSION_CARDS); the cap is FIXED — there is no user-configurable limit (a client-supplied limit is rejected)
sessions.semantics: startReviewSession snapshots the currently due card ids (ordered by due ascending, optional deckId filter) into a stable queue of at most 100 cards and records mode spaced_repetition, the EXACT dueCount captured at start, and continuationAvailable (true when more than 100 cards were due — after this session completes, start a NEW spaced-repetition session to cover the rest). submitSessionReview atomically applies FSRS scheduling to the expected current card AND advances the session (currentIndex/reviewedCount/ratingCounts/status) in ONE Firestore transaction, so retries/concurrency cannot double-apply a review or lose progress. Deleted snapshot cards are skipped automatically and the response always returns the next LIVE card (never card:null while cards remain). status: active -> completed (queue exhausted) or ended (abandoned via endReviewSession; idempotent). Sessions are scoped to the API key that started them: get/submit/end with a different key returns 403; submit on a non-active session returns 409. The response always includes the next card to review (null when the queue is exhausted).

dataModel.notes: Scheduling is implemented with the FSRS algorithm (ts-fsrs in functions/): new cards are created with due = creation time and state = New (0), and each review advances the card's due time through the FSRS scheduler. reviewFlashcard runs in a Firestore transaction so concurrent reviews are safe and no review log entry is lost. Timestamps are Firestore Timestamps returned as-is, serializing to { _seconds, _nanoseconds } (protobuf style) — verified against firebase-admin. listFlashcards returns { cards, nextPageToken } and filters tags with array-contains-any. dueFlashcards returns { cards, nextPageToken } ordered by due ascending. Bulk endpoints (bulkCreateFlashcardsHandler / bulkUpdateFlashcardsHandler / bulkDeleteFlashcardsHandler) mirror the single-card validation limits, are bounded at BULK_LIMIT=100 (functions/src/flashcards/types.ts), and commit atomically (Firestore batch/transaction — no partial silent success). The MCP server (mcp-server/src/tools.ts) normalizes these timestamps to ISO 8601 in its structuredContent. Decks are entities in a separate decks collection; cards reference them by stable deckId while the legacy denormalized deck name is preserved for readable/legacy filtering. Deck names are unique. deleteDeck is destructive to the deck only — cards are reassigned to Uncategorized (chunked batches, deck deleted only after reassignment batches succeed; partial reassignments on failure, retry is safe), never deleted. Card images are URL references only (never stored bytes); validated http(s) + allowed MIME/extension; max 5 per card; remove by exact URL removes only the reference. uploadImage stores bytes in Firebase Storage (default bucket) and persists only metadata on the card; remove deletes the Storage object for cloud images (best-effort) and card delete cleans up stored objects.

decks.delete_semantics: Deleting a deck NEVER deletes cards: every referencing card is REASSIGNED to Uncategorized (deckId/deck fields reassigned to Uncategorized) and the response reports reassignedCards. Reassignments run in chunked batches (<=500 writes each); the deck document is deleted only after all reassignment batches succeed. NOT a single atomic transaction: if a batch fails partway, earlier reassignments remain committed (the deck is not deleted) and retrying the delete is safe. Renaming a deck rewrites the deck name on its cards (also chunked).

images.model: CardImage { url, alt?, mimeType?, addedAt } stored on card.images
images.limits: max 5 images/card; upload decoded <= 10 MiB; base64 payload <= ~14 MiB; fileName <= 255; alt <= 500; upload MIME allowed: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp, image/avif, image/bmp (SVG NOT accepted for upload); URL attach allows http(s) + declared MIME or path extension incl. svg
images.semantics: External URL attachments: backend stores only the URL reference (never bytes). Cloud uploads: base64 bytes go to Firebase Storage under card-images/{cardId}/..., card stores id/storagePath/downloadUrl (signed URL)/contentType/sizeBytes/alt/addedAt. remove matches by exact URL (or id via url); for cloud images the Storage object is deleted best-effort. External hosted files are not deleted.

localTooling.notes: The mock server implements the exact contract in openapi.yaml (named-function routes, validation limits, auth, atomic bulk endpoints) so the schema and client can be exercised without a Firebase deployment. For the emulator, point the client at http://127.0.0.1:5001/<project-id>/us-central1.
